transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Carmen (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CTO, Aperture), Mark Chen (Lead ML Eng), Priya Nair (SRE), Omar Ruiz (Product)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
POC scoping focused on defining latency and throughput SLOs for Aperture's real-time summarization product. Discussed TTFT (time-to-first-token) vs TPOT (time-per-output-token), p95/p99 targets, bench plan, sample workload sizing, and timelines for a 3-week POC. Action items: Redwood to share benchmark harness and security docs; Aperture to share traffic traces and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone — thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena: Hi, Lena here, CTO at Aperture.
[00:07] Mark: Mark, ML eng.
[00:09] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:11] Omar: Omar, product.
[00:12] Maya: Great, Samir from our infra team?
[00:15] Samir: Hey all, Samir here, I'll be running the perf and bench bits. Carmen's on for success/ops.

[00:30] Maya: Goal for today is to scope a POC for latency/throughput SLOs — want to nail down success criteria, workload size, p95/p99 targets, and a measurement plan. We'll also align on timeline.

[01:02] Lena: High level — our product is low-latency real-time summarization of meeting transcripts for mobile clients. Typical requests are 300-800 tokens in, outputs 40-120 tokens. We need near-instant replies for the UI. We're sensitive to tail latency — p99 spikes are user-visible.

[01:36] Mark: To add, we have a global user base, about 200 QPS at peak across regions, but initial POC will only cover a 5-10 QPS representative slice. We want to understand Redwood Dedicated vs hosted options and tradeoffs for latency/cost.

[02:05] Samir: quick clarifying q — when you say p99 user visible, what's the threshold? Are we talking sub-200ms for first token? sub-500ms?

[02:18] Priya: For our mobile UX we target TTFT under 250ms p95, and p99 under 500ms ideally. For TPOT we want output token pacing such that generation doesn't exceed 60ms per token p95. If the model stalls it's bad.

[02:45] Maya: helpful. Let's define terms so we're aligned: TTFT (time-to-first-token) is from request arrival to when the first token is streamed to client. TPOT (time-per-output-token) is average time per generated token once generation starts. We usually measure p50/p95/p99 for both. We'll also measure end-to-end latency (request in to final token).

[03:20] Mark: Are these definitions the same as Redwood's? I've seen some docs call TPOT 'tokens per second' or 'throughput' — don't want metric mismatch.

[03:34] Samir: yeah, in our internal bench TPOT is measured as milliseconds per token; throughput is tokens/sec but they are convertible. For POC we'll publish both TPOT (ms/token) and throughput (tokens/sec) so everyone can map.

[04:05] Omar: question on workload sizing — Mark said peak 200 QPS company-wide. For POC we only give you a slice. What data do you need from us?

[04:20] Mark: We'll share request size distribution, percentiles for input tokens, typical output length, and concurrency patterns. For POC we'd give a representative 10 QPS steady load plus a 2-minute spike to 30 QPS to test autoscale/fallback.

[04:48] Maya: perfect. Also we need a sample corpus and a set of 20-30 benchmark prompts that represent the hard cases — long contexts, high generation length, and one-shot summary.

[05:10] Lena: we'll curate that and mark the 'golden' prompts the UX cares about.

[05:25] Samir: On measurement: we'll run two bench types — synthetic microbench with fixed token lengths to characterize TTFT/TPOT baseline per model variant, and an end-to-end replay using your sample traces to measure real traffic p95/p99. We'll instrument at request ingress and at token emission so we get TTFT and per-token timings.

[05:58] Priya: what's the measurement vantage? Are you running the collectors inside our VPC or via hosted? Security-wise we'd prefer the bench agent inside the VPC for private deployment testing.

[06:12] Samir: good point. For Private/VPC POC we can run the bench harness in your environment (we'll provide a small container). For Hosted tests we run from our infra; results are comparable but network jitter differs. We'll note that in the report.

[06:35] Maya: Let's draft the success criteria now. Suggested POC success criteria (tentative): 1) TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 500ms for representative 10 QPS load; 2) TPOT p95 <= 60ms/token and stable throughput >= X tokens/sec for the same load; 3) graceful degradation: when we spike to 30 QPS, 90% of requests should remain under TTFT p99 <= 1s with automatic fallback to smaller model variants if needed; 4) no data exfil in bench runs and security checks pass. Thoughts?

[07:30] Mark: Criteria 1 and 2 look good. For TPOT I'd like absolute throughput numbers too — maybe require sustained 1,500 tokens/sec at the cluster level on our sample workload. I need to check actual tokens/sec targets and convert from our product metrics.

[07:52] Priya: fallback behavior is key — we need documented policy and evidence of canary/rollback working. Also we want KV cache priming to be tested, since many summaries reuse context across requests. Is that supported?

[08:07] Samir: yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we'll include cache warmup scenarios. Note sometimes transcripts auto-transcribe 'KV' as 'kay vee' which confuses folks — but yes we test cache hit ratios.

[08:27] Omar: on model variants — do you recommend quantized variants for lower TPOT? Our team is worried about hallucination/regression risk.

[08:40] Samir: we typically recommend running a quality guardrail — run the same prompts across full-fp model and quantized model and compare ROUGE/BERTScore on a small eval set. For production you can tie quality regression alerts to specific prompt evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles. We'll include a compare-run in the POC.

[09:15] Maya: timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) — align on success criteria and sample data; week 1 — Redwood builds harness, customer provides traces and prompt set; week 2 — run microbench + analysis; week 3 — run replay tests + stability/spike tests + deliver report and recommendations. So roughly a 3-week POC. Is that viable?

[09:46] Lena: that's aggressive but acceptable if we keep scope to the 10 QPS slice and a single region. We can expand once we validate.

[10:00] Mark: is there infra setup time for Dedicated vs Hosted? If Dedicated requires reserved GPU pools it could add lead time.

[10:12] Maya: good call — Dedicated provisioning can take longer. For POC we usually either run hosted with provisioning for a comparable instance profile, or run a short-term dedicated eval node if the customer has reserved capacity. For Private/VPC setups we'll need around 3-5 business days to provision the bench container plus networking checks. We'll call that out.

[10:35] Priya: we need to ensure SSO and KMS policies are reviewed — we require encryption in transit and at rest for keys; Redwood's SOC2 is required.

[10:46] Carmen: we will share our SOC2, ISO docs and the security pack today (post-call). Also we'll redact any sensitive rows in the bench results if needed.

[11:02] Mark: instrumentation details — we want the raw per-request timing logs for analysis; can Redwood provide a CSV with timestamps and tokens emitted?

[11:11] Samir: yes, we'll deliver raw timing logs and a summary report with p50/p95/p99 for TTFT/TPOT and end-to-end latency, plus a breakdown by input size bucket. We'll also include concurrency and CPU/GPU utilization graphs.

[11:34] Omar: what about error modes — timeouts, OOMs? We need to define acceptable error budget for the POC.

[11:42] Maya: propose an error budget: <=1% failed requests (5xx) during steady 10 QPS window, and <=5% during spike test, excluding induced fallback. We can refine.

[11:58] Lena: ok. Also want to ensure cost estimates are provided — not a hard requirement to sign but we want to understand token cost and infra cost for each config.

[12:08] Maya: we'll include an estimated unit economics table in the POC report comparing hosted vs dedicated vs quantized variants.

[12:22] Mark: on measurement nuance — please be explicit how you measure TTFT: is it when first byte leaves server or when client ACKs the stream? Network RTT matters.

[12:34] Samir: we'll measure at the Redwood gateway side (server-side emit time) and also run a client-side probe in your VPC to capture full RTT. Report will show both server TTFT and client-observed TTFT. We'll annotate differences.

[13:00] Priya: for TPOT measurement do you average across tokens or report distribution?

[13:07] Samir: we'll report per-token percentiles and also a rolling mean ms/token. For output sequences we report median tokens/sec per-response and aggregate tokens/sec per-cluster.

[13:25] Maya: any blockers to proceed?

[13:31] Lena: none, just need the POC doc and security pack. We'll also need an NDA addendum for bench logs — legal will review.

[13:42] Maya: noted. We'll attach security docs and an abridged bench NDA.

[13:50] Omar: quick nit — I heard Samir say 'TTFT 250ms' — is that realistic on mobile? I'm concerned about mobile networks adding latency.

[13:59] Samir: that's why we run both server-site and client-side probes; for mobile we often see an extra 50-150ms RTT. The POC will surface that and we can recommend edge deployment or region routing to reduce RTT.

[14:22] Maya: ok let's recap next steps: 1) Redwood to send POC proposal + benchmark plan + security pack (Maya/Carmen) by 2026-07-23; 2) Aperture provides sample traces, prompt set, and tokens distribution by 2026-07-26 (Mark); 3) Redwood builds bench harness and shares scripts by 2026-07-28 (Samir); 4) Schedule 1-hour benchmark run week of 2026-08-03 (calendar invite to follow).

[14:58] Mark: confirmed. I'll start gathering traces.

[15:05] Lena: legal will follow up on NDA addendum.

[15:10] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc and set up the run.

[15:15] Carmen: thanks — notes and next steps will be in the follow-up email.

[15:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV' as 'kay vee', 'TTFT' read as 'tee tee eff tee' in a couple places). Speaker labels are as best guess from the recording.

End of transcript.
